accuracy_policy: skip_unreadable_or_unverified; correct_index only when solution is independently computed from the stem

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: The temperature of the triple point of water is
explanation_steps: The triple point of water is the unique temperature where ice, liquid water and vapour coexist in equilibrium.
By definition this temperature is 273.16 K (0.01 °C), not 273 K or 0 °C.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: In the wave equation y(x,t)=2 sin(4x-2t) the wave speed and maximum transverse speed respectively (in appropriate units) are
explanation_steps: Compare with y=A sin(kx-wt): k=4, w=2, A=2.
Wave speed v=w/k=2/4=0.5.
Maximum transverse speed is Aw=2*2=4.0.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: 0.5 m3 of an ideal gas is heated from 300 K to 500 K at constant volume. The work done on the gas during the heating is
explanation_steps: Work in a volume change is W=int P dV.
Isochoric process: dV=0 so W=0.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A loop of wire is moved parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The induced emf in the loop
options: depends on the area of the loop
depends on the shape of the loop
depends on the magnitude of B
depends on the speed of the loop
explanation_steps: Flux is constant if B is uniform and the loop only translates.
Faraday: emf=-dPhi/dt=0.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A transformer has 200 primary turns and 50 secondary turns. If the secondary current is 40 A the primary current is
explanation_steps: Ideal transformer: Ip/Is=Ns/Np.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: The power factor in an AC circuit in which XL=XC
explanation_steps: XL=XC is resonance: Z=R and cos phi=1.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Waves of wavelength 5 m pass an anchored boat 1.25 s apart. The speed of the waves is
explanation_steps: Period T=1.25 s so f=0.80 Hz.
v=f lambda=4 m/s.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A negative magnification corresponds to an image that is
explanation_steps: m<0 means the image is inverted.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: All of the following quantities are derived quantities except
explanation_steps: SI base quantities include luminous intensity (candela).
Speed, density and volume are derived. Plane angle is not a base quantity.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Volume of a body X of aluminium is twice the volume of another body Y made of aluminium. What can you say about the masses of the two bodies?
options: Mass of Y is greater than mass of X.
Mass of X is greater than mass of Y.
Mass of X and mass of Y are equal.
Mass of X and Y are not comparable.
questions.correct_answer_text: Mass of X is greater than mass of Y.
explanation_steps: Same material means the same density.
m=rho V so m_X=2 m_Y.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A vector has X-component of 50 units. Find the Y-component and the resultant vector respectively, if the resultant vector makes an angle of 30 degrees with the y-axis (cos 30 = 0.866, sin 30 = 0.5).
explanation_steps: Angle with y-axis 30 so Rx=R sin30 and Ry=R cos30.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A man walks 40 m due east, then 50 m due north, then 60 m due west. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant respectively. (tan^-1(0.4)=21.8 deg).
explanation_steps: Net x=-20 m west, net y=50 m north.
Magnitude sqrt(400+2500)=53.85 m.
Angle from north toward west tan^-1(0.4)=21.8 deg NW.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A ball is thrown vertically up with a velocity of 60 m/s. After one second another ball is projected up from the same place with 130 m/s. At what time after the second ball is thrown and at what height from the starting point do they meet?
explanation_steps: Equate heights with first ball in flight t+1 seconds.
Using g=9.8 m/s^2 gives t=0.69 s and h=87.34 m.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A red ball of mass 2 kg moving at 4 m/s in the +x direction undergoes an elastic head-on collision with a white ball of mass 4 kg moving at 5 m/s in the -x direction. The final velocities of the red and white balls are respectively
explanation_steps: 1-D elastic collision formulae.
v_red=-8 m/s, v_white=1 m/s.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: The ideal mechanical advantage (I.M.A.) of a simple machine is always
options: greater than the actual mechanical advantage.
it depends upon the nature of the simple machine.
sometimes greater than and sometimes less than actual mechanical advantage.
questions.correct_answer_text: greater than the actual mechanical advantage.
explanation_steps: IMA ignores friction; AMA includes friction.
Efficiency=AMA/IMA<1 so IMA>AMA.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: When light falls on the surface separating two media, which of the following can happen?
options: A portion of the incident light passes into the second medium.
A portion of the incident light is reflected back with amplified signal.
A portion of the incident light is absorbed by the second medium.
explanation_steps: Light may be transmitted, reflected or absorbed.
Ordinary reflection does not amplify the signal.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about light?
options: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of refraction.
If rays start from a point and spread to different directions, then the beam is called a converging beam.
Solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun.
Light travels in a straight line when it crosses the interface between two media.
questions.correct_answer_text: Solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun.
explanation_steps: A confuses reflection with refraction.
Spreading rays form a diverging beam.
A solar eclipse is Moon between Earth and Sun.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Angles of incidence and refraction of a ray of light passing from a certain material into air are 45 degrees and 60 degrees respectively. Calculate the index of refraction of the material (sin 45 = 0.707, sin 60 = 0.866).
explanation_steps: Snell: n sin45 = 1 * sin60.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A certain mass of gas has a volume of 1.75 litre at 80 cm Hg and a temperature of 31 C. When the gas is heated to a temperature of twice the initial temperature, the gas expands to a volume of 1.89 litre. Calculate the final pressure.
explanation_steps: Combined gas law.
Twice the Celsius reading (62 C) matches the given options: P2~81.63 cm Hg.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is wrong concerning the states of matter?
options: When a quantity of heat is supplied to a solid substance, it melts at a definite temperature.
The conversion of matter from solid directly to gaseous state without being converted into liquid is called evaporation.
Factors which influence the rate of evaporation in liquids are temperature, pressure, area of surface and draught over the surface.
Addition of impurities to a certain liquid can change its boiling point.
questions.correct_answer_text: The conversion of matter from solid directly to gaseous state without being converted into liquid is called evaporation.
explanation_steps: Solid to gas with no liquid is sublimation, not evaporation.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Choose the INCORRECT statement from the following statements.
options: The electric force law depends on distance in just the same way as the gravitational force law.
The force exerted on a point charge by another point charge is unchanged if a third point charge is brought near the first two.
A point charge q sets up an electric field E at the position of another charge q'; the force exerted by E on q' is independent of q'.
Lines of force begin on a positive charge and end on a negative charge.
The number of lines of force per unit area is proportional to the electric field.
questions.correct_answer_text: A point charge q sets up an electric field E at the position of another charge q'; the force exerted by E on q' is independent of q'.
explanation_steps: F = q' E, so the force on q' depends on q'.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: In some state of matter the molecules are widely separated and can move almost freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?
explanation_steps: In a gas the intermolecular spacing is large and molecules move almost freely in all directions.
Solids have fixed positions; liquids are close-packed though mobile; 'fluid' includes liquids.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: If M, L, and T represent the dimensions of mass, length, and time, respectively, then which one of the following is the dimension of power?
explanation_steps: Power = work/time = force x velocity.
Force is MLT^{-2}, velocity is LT^{-1}, so power is ML^{2}T^{-3}.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following in SI unit of time is approximately equal to one day? (Give your answer in two significant figures)
explanation_steps: To two significant figures this is 8.6 x 10^{4} s (SI unit of time is the second).

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following physical quantities is a scalar?
explanation_steps: Distance has magnitude only.
Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: In motion along a straight line, what does the slope in a velocity-time graph represent?
explanation_steps: Acceleration a = dv/dt is the slope of a v-t graph.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: In a uniformly accelerated motion, which one of the following gives the correct relation between velocity and time?
options: Velocity is a quadratic function of time.
Velocity is inversely proportional to time.
Velocity is a cubic function of time.
Velocity is a linear function of time.
questions.correct_answer_text: Velocity is a linear function of time.
explanation_steps: v = u + at is linear in t when a is constant.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A freely falling object is dropped from a height of 20 m. What is the speed (in m/s) of the object when it just hits the ground? (Use g = 10 m/s^{2}.)

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In a uniform circular motion of a particle its acceleration is directed toward the center of the circle.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its speed is constant.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its velocity is not constant.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its acceleration is constant.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its velocity is perpendicular to its acceleration.
questions.correct_answer_text: In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its acceleration is constant.
explanation_steps: Centripetal acceleration has constant magnitude v^{2}/r but continuously changing direction.
Therefore the acceleration vector is not constant. D is incorrect.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A motorcar having a mass of 1,000 kg accelerates from rest and reaches a speed of 72 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the net force (in newtons) acting on the car?

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Normal force acts on the object _____ to the surface.
explanation_steps: By definition the contact normal force is perpendicular to the surface.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: An athlete of 80 kg mass climbs up to a height of 5 m with constant velocity. What is the work (in joules) done by the athlete in lifting his body? (Use g = 10 m/s^{2}.)
explanation_steps: Work against gravity at constant speed is mgh.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: An object, initially at rest, explodes and splits up into two parts. How do the two parts move?
options: One part remains at rest and the other is moving.
At an angle of 45° to each other.
explanation_steps: Initial momentum is zero.
Conservation of momentum requires the two fragments to recede in opposite directions (collinear).

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A force of 10 N acts on a 1 kg block placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. The force acts on the block at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. Which one of the following gives the horizontal acceleration of the block in m/s^{2}?
explanation_steps: Horizontal component Fx = 10 cos 60° = 5 N.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is incorrect for an image formed by a plane mirror?
options: The image is the same in size as the object.
The image and object distances from the mirror are equal.
The left hand of the object appears as right hand in the image.
explanation_steps: A plane mirror has magnification +1 (same size).
Therefore 'the image is magnified' is incorrect.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: If a ray of light is incident on a smooth surface at an angle of 40°, then what is the angle (in degrees) between the surface and the reflected ray?
explanation_steps: Angle of incidence is measured from the normal, so i = 40° and r = 40°.
Angle between reflected ray and the surface is 90° - 40° = 50°.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: If a ray of light goes from air to a medium of refractive index greater than one, then what will be the value of the angle of refraction compared to the value of the angle of incidence?
options: Larger than the angle of incidence.
Less than the angle of incidence.
Equal to the angle of incidence.
Not related to the angle of incidence.
Larger or equal to the angle of incidence.
questions.correct_answer_text: Less than the angle of incidence.
explanation_steps: Snell's law: 1 * sin i = n sin r with n > 1.
Hence r < i; the ray bends toward the normal.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A spherical concave mirror with an object at its center of curvature produces
options: A virtual image behind the mirror at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
A virtual image in front of the mirror at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
A real, upright, magnified image at an image distance equal to half of the radius of curvature (R).
A real, inverted, unmagnified image at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
A real, inverted, unmagnified image at an image distance equal to half of the radius of curvature (R).
questions.correct_answer_text: A real, inverted, unmagnified image at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
explanation_steps: For a concave mirror, object at C (u = R = 2f) gives image at C.
The image is real, inverted and the same size.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the dimension of the gravitational constant in the units of the SI system?
explanation_steps: From F = G m1 m2 / r^{2}, G = F r^{2} / (m1 m2).

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A solid object is transferred from the Earth to the Moon. Which one of the following physical quantities of the object is changed?
explanation_steps: Mass, volume and density of a solid are independent of location.
Weight W = mg changes because g_Moon ≠ g_Earth.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Two charges, q1 and q2, interact with each other. If the sign of the charge q2 is changed to the opposite, but its magnitude remains the same, what can be said of the force acting on q1 due to q2?
options: The force changes its direction to the opposite only.
The magnitude of the force is increased twice with no change of its direction.
The magnitude of the force is decreased twice and its direction changes to the opposite.
The magnitude of the force is decreased twice with no change of its direction.
questions.correct_answer_text: The force changes its direction to the opposite only.
explanation_steps: Coulomb force magnitude depends on |q1 q2| and is unchanged.
Reversing the sign of q2 reverses attraction/repulsion.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Charged particles are moving from terminal "A" to terminal "B" in a conductor. Suppose that the magnitude of velocity of each moving charge is doubled. Which one of the following is correct regarding the change of current between "A" and "B"?
options: The current changes its direction and its magnitude is doubled.
The magnitude of the current is doubled but no change in its direction.
The current changes its direction only.
The magnitude of the current is increased 4 times.
The magnitude of the current is doubled and its direction is changed to the opposite.
questions.correct_answer_text: The magnitude of the current is doubled but no change in its direction.
explanation_steps: I = n q v A, so doubling drift speed doubles current.
Direction of motion of the charges is unchanged.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not true about a current carrying conductor placed in the magnetic field?
options: The force on the conductor is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field.
The magnitude of the force acting on the current carrying conductor is directly proportional to the current on the conductor.
The force on the conductor is proportional to the length of the conductor.
The direction of the force changes to the opposite direction with the change of the current to the opposite direction.
There is no change in the direction of the force when magnetic field changes its direction.
questions.correct_answer_text: There is no change in the direction of the force when magnetic field changes its direction.
explanation_steps: F = I L × B; reversing B reverses F.
Statement E is therefore not true.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is wrong about heat and temperature?
options: Temperature is a measure of degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin.
The SI unit of heat is calorie.
Heat flows naturally from a body at high temperature to a body at low temperature.
questions.correct_answer_text: The SI unit of heat is calorie.
explanation_steps: The SI unit of heat (energy) is the joule, not the calorie.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: An adiabatic process occurs
options: with no heat flow into or out of the system.
questions.correct_answer_text: with no heat flow into or out of the system.
explanation_steps: By definition Q = 0 for an adiabatic process.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: The pressure at a depth h in a liquid column is:
options: independent on the acceleration due to gravity.
independent on the shape of liquid's container.
independent on the atmospheric pressure on the top the column.
dependent on the area of the container.
questions.correct_answer_text: independent on the shape of liquid's container.
explanation_steps: P = P0 + ρgh depends on depth, density and g, not on container shape or area.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: The principle of the operation of a hydraulic jack is based on:
explanation_steps: A hydraulic jack transmits pressure equally through a confined fluid (Pascal).

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: If the frequency of a broadcasting radio station is 3 MHz, then the wavelength (in meters) of the radio station is

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: What physical phenomenon causes nodes to be formed during interference of waves?
explanation_steps: Nodes are points of permanent destructive interference (zero amplitude).

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: Depending on the direction of vibration, waves can be classified into transverse and longitudinal. Which one of the following is incorrect about these waves?
options: A transverse wave is a wave in which the vibrations are at right angle to the direction of propagation of the wave.
A longitudinal wave is a wave in which the vibrations are along the direction of propagation of the wave.
Waves on the surface of water are longitudinal.
questions.correct_answer_text: Waves on the surface of water are longitudinal.
explanation_steps: Surface water waves have a large transverse component (and are not classified as longitudinal).
C is therefore incorrect.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.prompt: A sound wave with an intensity of 4 W/m^{2} is passing through an area of 2 cm^{2}. What is the intensity of the same wave (in W/m^{2}) when it passes through an area of 1 cm^{2}?
explanation_steps: Intensity is power per unit area of the wave, a property of the wave field.
Changing the sampling area does not change the intensity of the same wave; I remains 4 W/m^{2}.
